description: An app that helps users generate customizable financial trackers (budget/expense/investment) exportable to Excel and/or Google Sheets.

questions.question: Which export target(s) should the generator support?
questions.rationale: Supporting both maximizes reach, but Google Sheets requires OAuth and a small backend while Excel export alone can be fully client-side.

options.label: Excel (.xlsx) export only
options.description: Generate and download an .xlsx file entirely in the browser, no backend required

options.label: Google Sheets integration only
options.description: Create a new Google Sheet directly in the user's Drive via OAuth + Sheets API

options.label: Both Excel and Google Sheets
options.description: Let users choose either export path

questions.question: What kind of financial tracker should be generated?
questions.rationale: An all-in-one template covers the most common personal finance use cases without much added complexity.

options.label: All-in-one (budget + expense + investment)
options.description: Combines budget, expense, and investment sheets/tabs

questions.question: What form should the application take?
questions.rationale: A web app has the lowest friction for users and works well with both client-side Excel generation and Google OAuth flows.

options.label: Web app (browser-based)
options.description: Accessible from any browser, easiest to deploy to Azure

questions.question: Do users need to sign in (e.g., to authorize Google Sheets access)?
questions.rationale: Only required if Google Sheets integration is selected; Excel-only export needs no sign-in.

options.label: Yes
options.description: Users sign in with Google to authorize Sheets creation

questions.question: What data storage does this app need?
questions.rationale: Tracker files can be generated and streamed directly to the user without server-side persistence.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: Server-side storage of generated files or templates

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Relational database for saved configurations or user accounts

questions.question: Which language should the frontend use?
questions.rationale: TypeScript gives better safety for form-driven template configuration logic.

questions.question: Which frontend framework should be used?
questions.rationale: React has the richest ecosystem for form builders, charts, and file-generation libraries (SheetJS, exceljs).

questions.question: Any specific features you want (e.g., custom budget categories, charts/graphs preview, multiple tracker templates, color themes)?
If a backend is needed (for Google OAuth/Sheets API), which language should it use?
questions.rationale: Keeping the same language as the frontend simplifies shared types and tooling.

questions.question: Anything specific the backend should handle beyond Google OAuth token exchange and creating/populating a Sheet (e.g., saving templates, rate limiting)?
